metadata.title: What matters for language learning? The questionnaire framework for the PISA 2025 Foreign Language Assessment

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD working paper is a questionnaire framework for the forthcoming PISA 2025 Foreign Language Assessment and does not report an analyzed student dataset. As such, it does not specify sampling weights, replicate weights, or any complex survey design variables for estimation. For later empirical PISA analyses using the resulting questionnaires, analysts should apply PISA’s standard complex survey design weights available in the international database (typically including student sampling weights and replicate weights) to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under stratification and clustering. The framework also notes that not all constructs will fit into the final questionnaires due to length restrictions, implying that measurement coverage (and thus analytic samples) will depend on which constructs are ultimately fielded.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This paper is a non-empirical questionnaire framework: it defines constructs and questionnaire content to be used alongside PISA 2025 foreign language proficiency results, but it does not estimate models on student-level cognitive outcomes. Because there is no dependent variable based on PISA cognitive achievement scores (and no reported PV-based analysis), plausible values handling is not applicable. Similarly, missing data handling is not reported because no analytic dataset, imputation strategy, or exclusion rule is implemented in this document.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student micro-data are analyzed in this framework paper. It describes how constructs will be selected and operationalized for PISA 2025 foreign language context questionnaires, including a policy-relevance determination process involving PISA-participating countries/economies and expert groups.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD working paper develops a questionnaire framework for the PISA 2025 Foreign Language Assessment, intended to collect policy and contextual information to interpret and produce policy-relevant analyses of 15-year-old students’ foreign language proficiency. The framework is organized around four policy domains—Government and school policies, Students and learning, Teachers’ training and profile, and Teaching practices—plus two transversal topics: ICT and the use of the target language for instruction in other subjects. It specifies construct definitions, expected relationships to foreign language learning, and the measurement levels (student, parent, teacher, school, system) for each construct. It also outlines a methodology for determining policy relevance (“essential” vs “relevant”) based on ratings by PISA-participating countries/economies and expert consensus. The paper does not provide empirical model results, benchmarks, or performance metrics; its contribution is the planned measurement architecture for future PISA 2025 analyses.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the document is a questionnaire framework and does not conduct an empirical analysis of PISA micro-data. Consequently, there is no analytic sample, no ML model training/evaluation, no PV-based outcome modeling, and no reported performance metrics. The main value is methodological: it defines constructs and their policy relevance to guide questionnaire development and later interpretation of PISA 2025 foreign language proficiency results.
